symptom: ako/mxcli#1769 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1673, 11.12.4): `alter microflow … { replace loop $Lookup in $Lookups with begin loop … begin $Line = find $Lines by Code = $Lookup/Code; … end loop; end; }`, $Lines retrieved over an association before the loop, stored the find as Microflows$FindByExpression `Code = $Lookup/Code`. check --references and exec reported nothing ("Altered microflow"), describe printed `find $Lines where Code = …`, mx check failed CE0117. create microflow writes Microflows$Find on MyModule.OrderLine.Code; the same find inserted on the main line was refused (#891's guard). `replace body of loop` had the same hole.
cause: Two. (1) #891's flowBuilder.qualifiedMembersOnly is set on the fragment's builder, but the loop, while and error-handler bodies are built by fresh flowBuilders whose fields each site listed by hand, and none listed the flag, so every member a nested body names (find/filter by member, sort, aggregate, change) at any depth was written bare. (2) alterFlowContext.storedVariables, the variables a fragment starts from, typed parameters, declares, creates, database retrieves and calls but left a retrieve over an association 'Unknown' (direction was the stated reason), so the member could not be qualified at all. Stored loop iterators were not typed either.
fix: flowBuilder.nestedBuilder is the one constructor for loop, while and error-handler bodies and inherits qualifiedMembersOnly with the rest of the shared state (the handler still adds returnType and labelReg). storedVariables types a retrieve over an association from its start variable through flowBuilder.associationRetrieveType (lookupAssociation + entityIsSubtypeOf + associationRetrieveYieldsList, the answer the full build and check take: from the TO end the list of the FROM entity, from the FROM end the TO object, a reference set a list either way, owner Both one object) and a loop's iterator from its list, to a fixed point so candidate order does not matter. A self-reference, an unknown association, or a name two loops or retrieves give different origins stays untyped and its member is refused.
test: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_nested_test.go TestNestedBuilder_InheritsSharedState (every flowBuilder field classified inherited or own, checked against nestedBuilder by reflection); flow_splice_nested_guard_test.go TestSpliceFragment_NestedBodiesRefuseUnqualifiedMembers (find/filter/sort/aggregate/change in loop, while, handler, loop in loop, handler in loop, while in handler, if in loop; typed control); flow_splice_assoc_retrieve_test.go (both directions, reference set, one-to-one, chain out of order, iterator, self-reference, ambiguous iterator); flow_splice_nested_guard_1769_pedapp_test.go (PedApp, real codec: replace loop, replace body, insert in body, insert on main line all write Microflows$Find; over an untyped list all four refused with nothing written; describe->exec Unchanged). Controls: flag left out of nestedBuilder -> every nested shape written and the structural test names the field; storedVariables reverted -> the reported shape refused; ambiguity guard off -> $ItOrder typed. Platform 11.13.0: unfixed CE0117 (1 error); fix (1) alone refused, exit 1, stored flow byte-identical; fixed Microflows$Find on MyModule.OrderLine.Code, mx check 0 errors, describe->exec Unchanged.
insight: A guard set on a builder is only as good as the places that construct builders: grep `&flowBuilder{` before trusting a flowBuilder flag, and where a field is copied by hand at several sites, replace the copies with one constructor and a test that makes every field be classified. The reported statement was not the blast radius: every member-writing statement in every nested body, and `replace body of`, had it. Separately, an unqualifiable member is the symptom of an untyped variable; read what the fragment's starting scope types (storedVariables) before adding another refusal. Check reports a fragment-builder refusal as 'not predicted' with the reason, not MDL090, as it does #891's main-line refusal.
